title: KCET 2021 Maths
subject: maths
source: KEA question paper (copy) + KEA answer key column A1

questions.q: In a certain town 65% families own cellphones, 15000 families own scooter and 15% families own both. Taking into consideration that the families own at least one of the two, the total number of families in the town is
questions.explanation: Since every family owns at least one, % owning scooter = 100 - 65 + 15 = 50%. So 50% of total = 15000, giving total = 30000.

questions.q: A and B are non-singleton sets and n(A $\times$ B) = 35. If B $\subset$ A then $^{n(A)}C_{n(B)}$ =
questions.explanation: n(A)n(B)=35=7$\times$5 with both >1, and since B$\subset$A, n(A)=7, n(B)=5, so $^7C_5$=21.

questions.q: Domain of f(x) = $\dfrac{x}{1-|x|}$ is
questions.explanation: The function is undefined when $|x|=1$, i.e. x = 1 or x = $-$1, so the domain is R $-$ {$-$1, 1}.

questions.q: The value of cos1200$^\circ$ + tan1485$^\circ$ is
questions.explanation: cos1200$^\circ$ = cos120$^\circ$ = $-1/2$ and tan1485$^\circ$ = tan45$^\circ$ = 1, so the sum is 1/2.

questions.q: The value of tan1$^\circ$ tan2$^\circ$ tan3$^\circ$ ............. tan89$^\circ$ is
questions.explanation: Pairing tan$k^\circ$ with tan(90$-k$)$^\circ$ gives products of 1 for k=1..44, and tan45$^\circ$=1, so the product is 1.

questions.q: If $\left(\dfrac{1+i}{1-i}\right)^{x}=1$ then
questions.explanation: (1+i)/(1-i) = i, and $i^x=1$ requires x to be a multiple of 4, so x = 4n, n$\in$N.

questions.q: The cost and revenue functions of a product are given by c(x) = 20x + 4000 and R(x) = 60x + 2000 respectively, where x is the number of items produced and sold. The value of x to earn profit is
questions.explanation: Profit requires R(x) > C(x): 60x+2000 > 20x+4000 $\Rightarrow$ 40x > 2000 $\Rightarrow$ x > 50.

questions.q: A student has to answer 10 questions, choosing at least 4 from each of the parts A and B. If there are 6 questions in part A and 7 in part B, then the number of ways the student can choose 10 questions is
If the middle term of the A.P is 300 then the sum of its first 51 terms is
questions.explanation: For 51 terms, the middle (26th) term equals the average term, so sum = 51 $\times$ 300 = 15300.

questions.q: The equation of straight line which passes through the point (a cos$^3\theta$, a sin$^3\theta$) and perpendicular to x sec$\theta$ + y cosec$\theta$ = a is
options: x cos$\theta$ $-$ y sin$\theta$ = a cos2$\theta$
x cos$\theta$ + y sin$\theta$ = a cos2$\theta$
questions.explanation: The given line has slope $-\tan\theta$, so the perpendicular has slope $\cot\theta$; using the point, the line simplifies to x cos$\theta$ $-$ y sin$\theta$ = a cos2$\theta$.

questions.q: The mid points of the sides of a triangle are (1, 5, $-$1), (0, 4, $-$2) and (2, 3, 4) then centroid of the triangle
questions.explanation: The centroid of a triangle equals the centroid of its midpoint triangle: averaging the three midpoints gives (1, 4, 1/3).

questions.q: Consider the following statements: Statement 1: $\displaystyle\lim_{x\to1}\dfrac{ax^2+bx+c}{cx^2+bx+a}$ is 1 (where a+b+c $\ne$ 0). Statement 2: $\displaystyle\lim_{x\to-2}\dfrac{\frac{1}{x}+\frac{1}{2}}{x+2}$ is $\dfrac{1}{4}$
questions.explanation: Statement 1: substituting x=1 gives (a+b+c)/(c+b+a)=1, true. Statement 2 simplifies to $\frac{1}{2x}$, which at x=$-$2 is $-1/4$, not $1/4$, so false.

questions.q: If a and b are fixed non-zero constants, then the derivative of $\dfrac{a}{x^4}-\dfrac{b}{x^2}$ + cosx is ma + nb $-$ p where
questions.explanation: Differentiating term by term: $-4a/x^5 + 2b/x^3 - \sin x$, matching m=$-4/x^5$, n=$2/x^3$, p=sinx.

questions.q: The Standard Deviation of the numbers 31, 32, 33 ........... 46, 47 is
questions.explanation: For n=17 consecutive integers, SD = $\sqrt{(n^2-1)/12}=\sqrt{288/12}=\sqrt{24}=2\sqrt6$.

questions.q: If P(A) = 0.59, P(B) = 0.30 and P(A $\cap$ B) = 0.21 then P(A' $\cap$ B') =
f : R $\to$ R defined by f(x) = 2x for x > 3; x$^2$ for 1 < x $\le$ 3; 3x for x $\le$ 1, then f($-$2) + f(3) + f(4) is
Let A = {x : x $\in$ R ; x is not a positive integer}. Define f : A $\to$ R as f(x) = $\dfrac{2x}{x-1}$, then f is
questions.explanation: The map $y=2x/(x-1)$ is one-one wherever defined, but since A excludes positive integers, some real y (whose pre-image is a positive integer) are never attained, so f is injective but not surjective.

questions.q: The function f(x) = $\sqrt3$ sin2x $-$ cos2x + 4 is one-one in the interval
questions.explanation: f(x) = 2sin(2x $-\pi/6$) + 4 is one-one when its argument lies in an interval of length $\pi$, giving x $\in$ [$-\pi/6$, $\pi/3$].

questions.q: Domain of the function f(x) = $\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{[x]^2-[x]-6}}$ where [x] is greatest integer $\le$ x is
questions.explanation: Need $([x]-3)([x]+2)>0$, i.e. [x] $\ge$ 4 or [x] $\le$ $-3$, which gives x $\in$ ($-\infty,-2)\cup[4,\infty)$.
cot$^{-1}(-\sqrt3) = 5\pi/6$; adding $\pi/6$ gives $\pi$, and cos$\pi = -1$.

questions.q: $\tan^{-1}\left[\dfrac{1}{\sqrt3}\sin\dfrac{5\pi}{2}\right] + \sin^{-1}\left[\cos\left(\sin^{-1}\dfrac{\sqrt3}{2}\right)\right] =$
questions.explanation: sin(5$\pi$/2) = sin($\pi$/2) = 1, so the first term is tan$^{-1}(1/\sqrt3)=\pi/6$. sin$^{-1}(\sqrt3/2)=\pi/3$, cos($\pi$/3)=1/2, so the second term is sin$^{-1}(1/2)=\pi/6$. Summing gives $\pi/3$; the operator between the two bracketed terms is unclear in the printed paper (a garbled '+' could be misread as no operator/multiplication), which is likely why KEA awarded grace marks to all four options.

questions.q: If A = $\begin{bmatrix}1 & -2 & 1\\ 2 & 1 & 3\end{bmatrix}$, B = $\begin{bmatrix}2 & 1\\ 3 & 2\\ 1 & 1\end{bmatrix}$ then (AB)' is equal to
questions.explanation: AB = $\begin{bmatrix}-3 & -2\\ 10 & 7\end{bmatrix}$, so its transpose (AB)' = $\begin{bmatrix}-3 & 10\\ -2 & 7\end{bmatrix}$.

questions.q: Let M be 2 $\times$ 2 symmetric matrix with integer entries, then M is invertible if
options: the first column of M is the transpose of second row of M
the second row of M is the transpose of first column of M
M is a diagonal matrix with non-zero entries in the principal diagonal
The product of entries in the principal diagonal of M is the product of entries in the other diagonal
questions.explanation: A diagonal matrix with non-zero diagonal entries has non-zero determinant (product of diagonal entries), so it is always invertible.

questions.q: If A and B are matrices of order 3 and |A| = 5, |B| = 3 then |3AB| is
questions.explanation: For a 3$\times$3 matrix, |3AB| = $3^3$|A||B| = 27 $\times$ 5 $\times$ 3 = 405.

questions.q: If A and B are invertible matrices then which of the following is not correct?
questions.explanation: The first three are standard matrix identities; (A+B)$^{-1}$ = B$^{-1}$+A$^{-1}$ is not a valid identity in general.

questions.q: If f(x) = $\begin{vmatrix}\cos x & 1 & 0\\ 0 & 2\cos x & 3\\ 0 & 1 & 2\cos x\end{vmatrix}$ then $\displaystyle\lim_{x\to\pi}f(x)$ =
questions.explanation: Expanding along the first column, f(x) = cosx(4cos$^2$x $-$3); at x=$\pi$, f($\pi$) = ($-1)(4-3)=-1$.

questions.q: If x$^3$ $-$ 2x$^2$ $-$ 9x + 18 = 0 and A = $\begin{vmatrix}1 & 2 & 3\\ 4 & x & 6\\ 7 & 8 & 9\end{vmatrix}$ then the maximum value of A is
questions.explanation: The cubic has roots x=2,3,$-$3, and A simplifies to $-12x+60$; evaluating at x=$-$3 gives the maximum value 96.

questions.q: At x = 1, the function f(x) = x$^3$ $-$ 1 for 1 < x < $\infty$, x $-$ 1 for $-\infty$ < x $\le$ 1 is
questions.explanation: Both one-sided limits and f(1) equal 0, so f is continuous; but the left derivative is 1 while the right derivative is 3, so it is not differentiable.

questions.q: If y = (cosx$^2$)$^2$, then dy/dx is equal to
For constant a, $\dfrac{d}{dx}(x^x + x^a + a^x + a^a)$ is
questions.explanation: Differentiating each term: $x^x(1+\log x)$, $ax^{a-1}$, $a^x\log a$, and 0 (a$^a$ is constant); summing gives option B.

questions.q: Consider the following statements: Statement 1: If y = log$_{10}$x + log$_e$x then dy/dx = $\dfrac{\log_{10}e}{x}+\dfrac{1}{x}$. Statement 2: $\dfrac{d}{dx}(\log_{10}x)=\dfrac{\log x}{\log 10}$ and $\dfrac{d}{dx}(\log_e x) = \dfrac{\log x}{\log e}$
options: Statement 1 is true; statement 2 is false
Statement 1 is false; statement 2 is true
questions.explanation: Statement 1 correctly gives dy/dx using the change of base rule; statement 2 wrongly states the derivative formulas (as per KEA key).

questions.q: If the parametric equation of a curve is given by x = cos$\theta$ + log tan($\theta$/2) and y = sin$\theta$, then the points for which dy/dx = 0 are given by
questions.explanation: dx/d$\theta$ = cos$^2\theta$/sin$\theta$ and dy/d$\theta$=cos$\theta$, so dy/dx = tan$\theta$, which is 0 when $\theta=n\pi$.

questions.q: If y = (x $-$ 1)$^2$(x $-$ 2)$^3$(x $-$ 3)$^5$ then dy/dx at x = 4 is equal to
questions.explanation: Using logarithmic differentiation, y'/y = 2/(x-1)+3/(x-2)+5/(x-3); at x=4, y=72 and y'/y=43/6, giving y'=516.

questions.q: A particle starts from rest and its angular displacement (in radians) is given by $\theta=\dfrac{t^2}{20}+\dfrac{t}{5}$. If the angular velocity at the end of t = 4 is k, then the value of 5k is
questions.explanation: $\omega=d\theta/dt=t/10+1/5$; at t=4, $\omega$=0.6=k, so 5k=3.

questions.q: If the parabola y = $\alpha$x$^2$ $-$ 6x + $\beta$ passes through the point (0, 2) and has its tangent at x = 3/2 parallel to x axis, then
questions.explanation: Passing through (0,2) gives $\beta$=2; the tangent slope 2$\alpha$x$-$6=0 at x=3/2 gives $\alpha$=2.

questions.q: The function f(x) = x$^2$ $-$ 2x is strictly decreasing in the interval
questions.explanation: f'(x) = 2x $-$ 2 < 0 gives x < 1, so f is strictly decreasing on ($-\infty$, 1).

questions.q: The maximum slope of the curve y = $-$x$^3$ + 3x$^2$ + 2x $-$ 27 is
questions.explanation: Slope y' = $-3x^2+6x+2$; maximizing gives x=1, so maximum slope = $-3+6+2=5$.

questions.q: $\displaystyle\int\dfrac{x^3\sin(\tan^{-1}(x^4))}{1+x^8}dx$ is equal to
questions.explanation: Substituting u = tan$^{-1}(x^4)$, du = $4x^3/(1+x^8)dx$, the integral becomes $-\cos u/4+C$.

questions.q: The value of $\displaystyle\int\dfrac{x^2dx}{\sqrt{x^6+a^6}}$ is equal to
questions.explanation: Substituting u = x$^3$, du = 3x$^2$dx, the integral becomes $\frac13\log|x^3+\sqrt{x^6+a^6}|+c$.

questions.q: The value of $\displaystyle\int\dfrac{xe^x dx}{(1+x)^2}$ is equal to
questions.explanation: Since $\frac{d}{dx}\left[\frac{e^x}{1+x}\right]=\frac{xe^x}{(1+x)^2}$, the integral is $\dfrac{e^x}{1+x}+c$.

questions.q: The value of $\displaystyle\int e^x\left[\dfrac{1+\sin x}{1+\cos x}\right]dx$ is equal to
questions.explanation: $\frac{1+\sin x}{1+\cos x}=\tan(x/2)+\frac12\sec^2(x/2)$, which is of the form f(x)+f'(x) with f(x)=tan(x/2), giving $e^x\tan(x/2)+c$.

questions.q: If $I_n=\displaystyle\int_0^{\pi/4}\tan^n x\,dx$ where n is a positive integer, then $I_{10}+I_8$ is equal to
The value of $\displaystyle\int_0^{4042}\dfrac{\sqrt x\,dx}{\sqrt x+\sqrt{4042-x}}$ is equal to
questions.explanation: Using $\int_0^a f(x)dx=\int_0^a f(a-x)dx$, twice the integral equals 4042, so the integral is 2021.

questions.q: The area of the region bounded by y = $\sqrt{16-x^2}$ and x $-$ axis is
questions.explanation: This curve is the upper half of a circle of radius 4, so the correctly bounded area is $8\pi$ sq units, which is not among the printed options; KEA awarded grace marks for this defective question (closest listed option taken here is 16$\pi$).

questions.q: If the area of the Ellipse $\dfrac{x^2}{25}+\dfrac{y^2}{\lambda^2}=1$ is 20$\pi$ square units, then $\lambda$ is
questions.explanation: Area of ellipse = $\pi ab = \pi(5)|\lambda|=20\pi$, giving $|\lambda|=4$, so $\lambda=\pm4$.

questions.q: Solution of Differential Equation xdy $-$ ydx = 0 represents
options: Parabola whose vertex is at origin
A circle whose centre is origin
questions.explanation: Separating variables, dy/y = dx/x, giving y = kx, a straight line through the origin.

questions.q: The number of solutions of $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=\dfrac{y+1}{x-1}$ when y(1) = 2 is
questions.explanation: The initial point x=1 is a singular point of the equation (denominator vanishes there); KEA's key accepts both 'one' and 'infinite' as correct.

questions.q: A vector $\vec a$ makes equal acute angles on the coordinate axis. Then the projection of vector $\vec b$ = 5$\hat i$ + 7$\hat j$ $-\hat k$ on $\vec a$ is
questions.explanation: Equal acute angles give direction cosines $1/\sqrt3$ each; projection = $\vec b\cdot\hat a=(5+7-1)/\sqrt3=11/\sqrt3$.

questions.q: The diagonals of a parallelogram are the vectors 3$\hat i$ + 6$\hat j$ $-2\hat k$ and $-\hat i-2\hat j-8\hat k$ then the length of the shorter side of parallelogram is
questions.explanation: The sides are half the sum and difference of the diagonals; as printed this gives lengths $\sqrt{30}$ and $\sqrt{29}$, matching none of the options exactly (apparent sign typo in the question), so KEA awarded grace marks. Taking the likely-intended diagonal, the shorter side works out to $\sqrt{14}$.

questions.q: If $\vec a\cdot\vec b$ = 0 and $\vec a+\vec b$ makes an angle 60$^\circ$ with $\vec a$ then
questions.explanation: cos60$^\circ = |\vec a|/|\vec a+\vec b| = 1/2$, so $|\vec a+\vec b|=2|\vec a|$; since $\vec a\cdot\vec b=0$, $|\vec a+\vec b|^2=|\vec a|^2+|\vec b|^2$ gives $|\vec b|=\sqrt3|\vec a|$.

questions.q: If the area of the parallelogram with $\vec a$ and $\vec b$ as two adjacent sides is 15 sq. units then the area of the parallelogram having 3$\vec a$+2$\vec b$ and $\vec a$+3$\vec b$ as two adjacent sides in sq. units is
questions.explanation: $(3\vec a+2\vec b)\times(\vec a+3\vec b)=7(\vec a\times\vec b)$, so the new area = 7 $\times$ 15 = 105.

questions.q: The equation of the line joining the points ($-$3, 4, 11) and (1, $-$2, 7) is
questions.explanation: Direction ratios are (4,$-$6,$-$4), i.e. (2,$-$3,$-$2) or equivalently ($-$2,3,2), giving the equation in option B.

questions.q: The angle between the lines whose direction cosines are $\left(\dfrac{\sqrt3}{4},\dfrac14,\dfrac{\sqrt3}{2}\right)$ and $\left(\dfrac{\sqrt3}{4},\dfrac14,\dfrac{-\sqrt3}{2}\right)$ is
questions.explanation: cos$\theta$ = 3/16+1/16$-$3/4 = $-1/2$; taking the acute angle between the lines (absolute value), $\theta=\pi/3$.

questions.q: If a plane meets the coordinate axes at A, B and C in such a way that the centroid of triangle ABC is at the point (1, 2, 3) then the equation of the plane is
questions.explanation: With intercepts p,q,r, centroid = (p/3,q/3,r/3) = (1,2,3) gives p=3,q=6,r=9, so the plane is x/3+y/6+z/9=1.

questions.q: The area of the quadrilateral ABCD, when A(0, 4, 1) B(2, 3, $-$1) C(4, 5, 0) and D(2, 6, 2) is equal to
questions.explanation: Area = $\frac12|\vec{AC}\times\vec{BD}| = \frac12|(6,-12,12)| = \frac12(18)=9$ sq. units.

questions.q: The shaded region is the solution set of the inequalities [graph shows the line 5x+4y=20 through (0,5) and (4,0), with the lines x=6 and y=3, and the shaded region between these boundaries]
questions.explanation: The shaded region lies on the far side of the line 5x+4y=20 from the origin, bounded also by x $\le$ 6 and y $\le$ 3 (as per KEA key).

questions.q: Given that A and B are two events such that P(B) = 3/5, P(A/B) = 1/2 and P(A $\cup$ B) = 4/5, then P(A) =
If A, B and C are three independent events such that P(A) = P(B) = P(C) = P then P(at least two of A, B, C occur) =
questions.explanation: P(exactly two) + P(all three) = $3P^2(1-P)+P^3 = 3P^2-2P^3$.

questions.q: Two dice are thrown. If it is known that the sum of numbers on the dice was less than 6 the probability of getting a sum as 3 is
questions.explanation: Outcomes with sum < 6: 1+2+3+4 = 10 (for sums 2,3,4,5); outcomes with sum 3 = 2; probability = 2/10 = 1/5.

questions.q: A car manufacturing factory has two plants X and Y. Plant X manufactures 70% of cars and plant Y manufactures 30% of cars. 80% of cars at plant X and 90% of cars at plant Y are rated as standard quality. A car is chosen at random and is found to be of standard quality. The probability that it has come from plant X is
